name: Clomiphene / enclomiphene
lead: Clomiphene (clomifene, brand Clomid) is an oral selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) approved for treating ovulatory dysfunction in women [1][2]. In men it is used off-label by prescribers to raise the body's own testosterone, and it is discussed in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing communities as a way to raise testosterone without testosterone injections or to restart natural production after steroid cycles [1][3]. The appearance chain people describe is higher testosterone, then more energy, training capacity, muscle, leaner body composition and the broader features associated with testosterone, such as skin, hair and facial development; enthusiasts also discuss it as a route to 'testosterone maxxing' in younger users [3][14].

Clomiphene is a mixture of roughly 62 percent enclomiphene and 38 percent zuclomiphene isomers [1][4]. Enclomiphene, the more antiestrogenic isomer, was developed as a purified drug for men with secondary hypogonadism. Its developer received an FDA Complete Response Letter in December 2015, the EMA committee recommended refusing authorisation in January 2018, and development was discontinued in April 2021 [4][15].

Trials and meta-analyses in hypogonadal men report raised testosterone, LH and FSH and, for clomiphene, improved symptom scores and sperm parameters [16][17][18]. Reported adverse effects include visual symptoms, and the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits clomiphene [1][2]. No published trial was found testing either drug for facial or appearance outcomes.

paras: The US label states clomiphene citrate is indicated for ovulatory dysfunction in women desiring pregnancy, including those with polycystic ovary syndrome [2]. Randomized trials have compared it with metformin and letrozole for infertility in PCOS [5][6]. In clinical practice it has also been used in men with low testosterone as an alternative to testosterone replacement, and it has been tried in gynecomastia, though Wikipedia says it is not recommended for that [1]. It has also been used to restore sperm production in trans women who wish to have biological children, according to Wikipedia [1].

For men with secondary hypogonadism, SERMs offer an option that raises testosterone through the brain's own signalling and, unlike testosterone replacement, does not suppress sperm production in the way exogenous testosterone does [16][17]. Systematic reviews describe clomiphene as off-label therapy for this purpose [16]. In a 2022 meta-analysis of 19 studies (1,642 patients), total testosterone, free testosterone, LH, FSH, SHBG and estradiol all rose during treatment, symptom scores improved, side effects occurred in fewer than 10 percent of study populations and no serious adverse events were reported [16]. A 2023 meta-analysis of clomiphene for male infertility (15 studies, n=566) found higher sperm concentration and motility during treatment and no change in morphology [17].

Wikipedia gives study figures such as testosterone rising from about 309 to 642 ng/dL in men with low baseline levels treated for three months, and notes that lipid, glucose and prolactin levels did not change significantly, though total cholesterol decreased [1].

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities
paras: On looksmax.org, users discuss enclomiphene as a way to increase testosterone, as an add-on to steroid or other compound regimens, and as a post-cycle option; some posters cite a 2024 study comparing clomiphene and enclomiphene as showing larger testosterone increases and fewer side effects for enclomiphene [3]. Thread titles include a 'complete guide to testosterone maxxing' aimed at young users and questions about using it in the mid-teens [14][19][20]. Other threads discuss fatigue or feeling unwell after taking it and whether growth plates remain open [21][19]. One reply in a thread on bone growth said testosterone and DHT would not grow bones by themselves and that growth hormone was the route for that [22].

On T Nation, users discuss clomiphene in the context of low testosterone, fertility and recovery after steroid cycles, and post-cycle therapy is a recurring topic [23]. These forum reports are anecdotal and describe individuals' experiences.

Clomiphene blocks estrogen's negative feedback in the hypothalamus, increasing GnRH pulses and raising LH and FSH, which stimulates ovulation in women and testicular testosterone production in men [1]. It acts as an ER-alpha agonist when estrogen is low and a partial blocker when estrogen is high, and it antagonises ER-beta [1]. It is a prodrug whose active metabolites form via CYP2D6, and variants in that enzyme produce wide differences in response [1]. Enclomiphene is described as pro-androgenic and zuclomiphene as pro-estrogenic with a half-life of days to a week, so ordinary clomiphene may produce longer-lasting estrogenic than androgenic effects [1][4]. Enclomiphene raises total and free testosterone without a disproportionate rise in DHT [4].

Oral bioavailability is over 90 percent and clomiphene is metabolised mainly in the liver with enterohepatic recirculation and mostly faecal excretion; effects begin 5 to 10 days after starting treatment in ovulation induction. Clomiphene's half-life is about 4 to 7 days, and zuclomiphene can be detected in urine for at least 261 days after stopping. Enclomiphene's half-life is about 10 hours [1][4].
Clomiphene is a triphenylethylene derivative (formula C26H28ClNO) that exists as two geometric isomers; the US Pharmacopeia requires 30 to 50 percent zuclomiphene in the citrate mixture [1].

Registered phase 3 trials include enclomiphene in men with secondary hypogonadism (n=104, n=300 extension, and n=499 safety study) [7][8][9]. A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis of clomiphene in hypogonadal men (19 studies, 4 randomized and 15 observational, 1,642 patients) reported rises in total testosterone and in LH and FSH, improved ADAM symptom scores, side effects in under 10 percent of populations and no serious adverse events [16]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials of clomiphene or enclomiphene reported that SERMs raised total testosterone by a mean of about 274 ng/dL versus placebo, with LH and FSH also higher, and that total testosterone did not differ significantly from testosterone gel; the authors suggested SERMs be considered as an alternative to gel therapy [18].

Fertility endpoints have been studied too. The 2023 male infertility meta-analysis found higher sperm concentration (mean difference 8.38 million per mL) and motility (8.14 percentage points) during treatment, with a mean pregnancy rate of 17 percent across ten studies [17]. Wikipedia reports a pooled safety population of 1,403 participants for enclomiphene [4].

Large trials in women include NEJM comparisons of clomiphene with metformin and with letrozole for PCOS infertility [5][6]. No studies were found of either drug for facial appearance, muscle or body-composition outcomes in healthy men. Reports on healthy men cited by Wikipedia (50 mg per day for eight months) described large testosterone rises, but these are small studies and not appearance trials [1].

In the US label's clinical-trial data, ovarian enlargement (13.6 percent) and vasomotor flushes (10.4 percent) were most common; visual symptoms including blurring and scotomata occasionally occur and increase with total dose or duration, and may rarely be prolonged or irreversible [2]. Use in pregnancy is contraindicated [2]. Wikipedia also lists headaches, hot flashes and abdominal discomfort as common, with rarer reports of liver inflammation, reversible hair loss and high triglycerides, plus some liver abnormalities and rare hepatotoxicity [1].

In men, trial populations report fewer adverse events than in women, but forum users describe fatigue, mood changes and estrogen-related symptoms on clomiphene [16][21]. Zuclomiphene's long half-life means estrogenic effects may persist for weeks [1].

For enclomiphene, pooled data from 1,403 trial participants reported headache (1.6 percent), hot flush (1.1), nausea (1.0) and muscle spasms (0.9), with rarer deep vein thrombosis (0.2), pulmonary embolism (0.1) and one fatal ischemic stroke; as a SERM it is associated with thromboembolic risk [4]. Contraindications include pregnancy, breastfeeding and liver disease history [4].

Clomiphene was synthesized in 1956 by a team led by Frank Palopoli at William S. Merrell Chemical Company, patented in November 1959, and approved in the US in 1967 as Clomid, the third drug filed under the 1962 Kefauver-Harris Amendment [1]. It was studied for advanced breast cancer from 1964 to 1974 (34 percent response rate) and abandoned for that use as tamoxifen emerged [1]. It became the most widely prescribed ovulation-induction drug and is on the WHO Essential Medicines List; economist Eli Adashi described its role in the US multiple-births epidemic [1].

Enclomiphene (tentative names Androxal and EnCyzix) was developed by Repros Therapeutics for male secondary hypogonadism. On 1 December 2015 the company announced an FDA Complete Response Letter for its NDA in overweight men with secondary hypogonadism; the FDA said the design of the phase 3 studies was no longer adequate to demonstrate clinical benefit and asked for another trial, and also raised concerns about entry criteria and titration [15]. CEO Joseph Podolski said the company was disappointed the FDA acted without an advisory committee [15]. In January 2018 the EMA's CHMP recommended refusing marketing authorisation, and development was discontinued in April 2021 [4].

Clomiphene is prescription-only in the US, UK and Australia and is marketed worldwide under more than 100 brand names [1]. Enclomiphene has no regulatory approval for any indication, and gray-market and compounded products are discussed in online communities; [4]. WADA prohibits clomiphene (category S4), and it can be an undeclared ingredient in black-market products; athletes have also tested positive via contaminated food, and WADA has developed a method to distinguish dietary exposure from doping [1].

Prescribers and telehealth clinics offer clomiphene and enclomiphene preparations for low testosterone; there are no peer-reviewed analyses of prescribing trends, and the marketing claims come from sellers.

Alternatives discussed alongside SERMs include testosterone replacement therapy, human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) to maintain testicular function, tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors for estrogen management [1][23]. Post-cycle therapy (PCT), the use of SERMs after anabolic steroid cycles to restore natural testosterone production, is a recurring forum topic [23].

lore.intro: Clomiphene and enclomiphene are discussed as ways to boost endogenous testosterone, as post-cycle options and, among younger users, as 'testosterone maxxing' [3][14].

claims.claim: Enclomiphene raises testosterone more than clomiphene with fewer side effects
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster cited a September 2024 comparison as showing enclomiphene boosted testosterone more with fewer side effects, and another user called it a solid add-on to other compound regimens [3].
claims.experts: Reference sources describe enclomiphene as the more androgenic isomer reported to be about twice as effective as the mixture, while zuclomiphene is pro-estrogenic [1]; it was not approved by regulators [4].

claims.claim: These drugs raise testosterone without testosterone replacement
claims.believers: Users describe them as stimulating the body's own production.
claims.experts: Trials and reviews report increased testosterone and preserved sperm counts in men with secondary hypogonadism [4]; clomiphene is off-label for men [1].

claims.claim: Enclomiphene is a 'magic drug' for young men's testosterone
claims.believers: A thread titled as a complete guide to testosterone maxxing for 'pubertycels' presents enclomiphene as a way for young men to raise testosterone [14].
claims.experts: Trials enrolled adult men with secondary hypogonadism; no published trial has tested it in adolescents or for appearance outcomes [7][8][9].

claims.claim: Testosterone boosters can extend growth or 'bone-maxx'
claims.believers: A thread asks about enclomiphene for height and bone growth, and another asks about growth plates at 16 [22][19].
claims.experts: Replies in the threads say testosterone and DHT will not grow bones by themselves and that plates are mostly closed by then; no published trial has examined enclomiphene for height [22][19].

claims.claim: Clomiphene is useful for restarting the body after steroid cycles
claims.believers: T Nation posters discuss clomiphene for PCT and fertility after blasts and cruises [23].
claims.experts: Studies in men with hypogonadism report raised testosterone and LH, and preserved sperm parameters; trials have not tested post-steroid recovery specifically [16][17].

claims.claim: Clomiphene or enclomiphene causes side effects like fatigue and low libido
claims.believers: Users report feeling unwell or sleepy after taking enclomiphene, and a T Nation thread describes high testosterone but low libido on clomiphene [21][25].
claims.experts: The 2022 meta-analysis reported side effects in under 10 percent of study populations; the label lists visual symptoms among documented adverse effects of clomiphene [16][2].

claims.claim: Enclomiphene is safer than clomiphene because it avoids zuclomiphene
claims.believers: The 2024 forum comparison is cited as showing fewer side effects for enclomiphene [3].
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes zuclomiphene as pro-estrogenic with a long half-life, but no head-to-head randomized trial in men was found, and enclomiphene was refused approval in the EU [1][4].

card.summary: A fertility SERM used off-label by men to raise their own testosterone; trial data in hypogonadal men, none for looks.
card.note: Prescription-only; visual disturbances reported; WADA-prohibited; enclomiphene never approved.

quick.overview:
Clomiphene is an oral fertility drug that men also use off-label to raise their own testosterone. Enclomiphene is its more androgenic isomer.

Trials in men with secondary hypogonadism report testosterone rises. No studies were found on appearance outcomes.
quick.mechanism: It blocks estrogen feedback in the brain, increasing LH and FSH signals that drive testicular testosterone production.
quick.risks: The label lists ovarian enlargement and flushes in women, and visual symptoms that can occasionally be prolonged. Enclomiphene was refused EU authorization in 2018. Clomiphene is prescription-only and WADA-prohibited.

chain: Blocks estrogen feedback in the brain
Users aim for more training capacity, muscle and leaner body composition
angle.text: Clomiphene and enclomiphene are used by men to raise their own testosterone while leaving the testes working, which people hope translates into muscle, leanness and the general look associated with higher testosterone. In bodybuilding circles they are also used to restart natural production after steroid cycles.
